mainTopic: How ledges, ladders and stakes change the status of walls and pillars: lowering a wall between courtyards, and cancelling a pillar's status as a רשות היחיד.
overview: A wall at least ten טפחים high fully separates two courtyards. This amud asks when a ledge (זיז) or a ladder (סולם) makes such a wall count as lower, so people can cross it. A 4-by-4 זיז with a ladder leading onto it lowers the wall, and a 20-טפח wall needs two staggered זיזים. In the middle, the גמרא turns to a pillar in רשות הרבים: does a stake driven into its top cancel its status as a רשות היחיד? רב אדא, אביי and רבא, and רב אשי each give a different answer, and רב אשי proves his view from רבי יוחנן's rule about a pit and its rim. Next, אמוראים argue about how long a ladder must be for a ten-טפח wall, from fourteen טפחים down to seven and a bit if it stands upright. שמואל explains רב's tradition that even an upright ladder counts. The amud ends with heavy Babylonian palm trunks and ladders that count as fixed in place. Last is רבה's test for combined ladders: they count only if the foot can climb in the middle.

steps.title: A ledge with a ladder lowers the wall
steps.stepSummary: If a 4-by-4 זיז sticks out of the wall and a ladder of any width leads up to it, the wall's height counts as reduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ledge that sticks out of the wall, four טפחים by four טפחים, with a ladder of any size placed against it, lowers the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: a ledge that is large enough to stand on, together with a ladder leading up to it, counts as lowering the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 4-by-4 זיז is a real standing place, so the ladder reaching it does not need any minimum width. Once you can climb onto the זיז, the wall is measured from the זיז upward. If that remaining part is less than ten טפחים, the wall no longer fully separates the courtyards.

keyTerms.meaning: A ledge or projection sticking out of a wall
Four by four טפחים, the minimum size of a significant standing place
He has reduced it, meaning the wall's effective height

steps.confusionAlert: 'מיעטו' does not mean the wall is physically shorter. It means that, halachically, the wall's height is now measured from the זיז, which a person can reach by the ladder.

phrases.english: A ledge that sticks out from the wall
and he placed against it a ladder of any width
he has reduced it (the wall's height)
phrases.notes: The ladder lets a person reach the ledge, so the wall is measured from there.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִיז הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַכּוֹתֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the larger sugya about lowering a ten-טפח wall between courtyards.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 4-by-4 זיז with a ladder of any width leading to it reduces the wall's effective height.

steps.title: The ladder must lead onto the ledge, not stand beside it
steps.stepSummary: The rule only works if the ladder reaches up onto the זיז. A ladder placed next to the זיז just makes the ledge wider.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he placed the ladder leading onto the ledge. But if he placed it next to the ledge, he has only widened the ledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the rule it just gave: the ladder has to lead up to the זיז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the ladder is placed 'עליה', you can climb from the ground onto the זיז, so the זיז is connected to the ground. When it is placed 'בהדיה', beside the זיז, it only adds to the ledge's width. Nothing leads up to it, so it cannot lower the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when..., a formula that limits a previous statement
He set it against it, so the ladder leads onto the ledge

steps.whatToRemember: A זיז lowers the wall only when a ladder actually lets a person climb onto it.

phrases.english: where he set the ladder leading onto the ledge
but if he set it next to the ledge

phrases.notes: The ledge is still out of reach from the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּאוֹתְבֵיהּ עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows step 1 by defining which ladder placement counts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a ladder that leads onto the זיז lowers the wall; one placed beside it only widens the זיז.

steps.title: A nineteen-handbreadth wall needs one ledge
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, rules that a wall 19 טפחים high can be made passable with one זיז.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: a wall nineteen טפחים high needs one ledge to make it permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement that applies the זיז-and-ladder idea to a very tall wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a 19-טפח wall, one זיז in the middle can be less than ten טפחים from the ground and less than ten from the top. A ladder brings you onto the זיז, and from there the rest of the wall is under ten. That one זיז is therefore enough.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who transmits this ruling
The teacher רב נחמן is quoting
To make it permitted, so the wall no longer fully separates the courtyards

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
needs one ledge to make it permitted

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the זיז rule with a related new statement about tall walls.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 19-טפח wall is made permitted with one זיז.

steps.title: A twenty-handbreadth wall needs two ledges
steps.stepSummary: A wall 20 טפחים high needs two זיזים: one within ten טפחים of the ground and one within ten of the top.
steps.simpleTranslation: A wall twenty טפחים high needs two ledges to make it permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The same statement continues and covers a wall just one טפח taller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a 20-טפח wall, a single זיז cannot be less than ten טפחים from both the ground and the top. At best, each gap would be exactly ten, which still counts as separating. So two זיזים are needed to break the height into gaps of under ten.
steps.confusionAlert: Ten טפחים is already a full separating wall. The gap must be less than ten, which is why one extra טפח forces a second זיז.

phrases.english: needs two ledges to make it permitted

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוֹתֶל עֶשְׂרִים צָרִיךְ שְׁנֵי זִיזִים לְהַתִּירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of רבה בר אבוה's ruling, contrasting a 20-טפח wall with a 19-טפח wall.

steps.title: The two ledges must not be directly one above the other
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds that the two זיזים only work if they are staggered, not stacked in a straight line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: this only works when he set them up so that one is not directly above the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a condition to the two-ledge rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To climb from the lower זיז to the upper one, a ladder must stand on the lower זיז and reach the upper one. If the upper זיז sits directly overhead, it blocks the way up and there is no room to climb onto it. Staggering them makes a real climbing path.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who adds a condition
And this applies only when..., a formula that adds a condition
Not directly opposite or above each other

steps.whatToRemember: A זיז lowers a wall only when a person can actually climb onto it. That is why the ladder must lead onto it, a 20-טפח wall needs two זיזים, and the two must be staggered.

phrases.english: And this applies only when he set them up
so that one is not directly above the other

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא וְהוּא שֶׁהֶעֱמִידָן זֶה שֶׁלֹּא כְּנֶגֶד זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the two-ledge rule in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two זיזים on a 20-טפח wall must be staggered so a person can climb from one to the other.

steps.title: A stake of any size reduces a pillar's surface
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא: a stake of any size driven into a 4-by-4, 10-high pillar in רשות הרבים takes away its status as a full surface.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If a pillar in רשות הרבים is ten טפחים high and four wide, and someone drove a stake of any size into it, he has reduced it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a new rule. Driving even a tiny stake into the top of a large pillar 'reduces' the pillar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pillar 10 טפחים high and 4-by-4 wide counts as its own רשות היחיד, even when it stands in רשות הרבים. A stake breaks up the 4-by-4 surface, so the pillar no longer has a full usable area. That means it loses its status as a רשות היחיד.

keyTerms.meaning: He reduced it (here: reduced its usable area)

steps.confusionAlert: In the earlier steps, 'reducing' meant making a wall count as lower. Here מיעטו means making the pillar's usable surface count as smaller than 4-by-4. The goal is also the opposite: before, we wanted to make a wall passable, and here the pillar loses its status as a רשות היחיד.

phrases.english: A pillar in the public domain,
ten handbreadths high and four wide,
phrases.notes: These measurements make it a private domain.

phrases.english: and he drove into it a stake of any size —

phrases.notes: Its usable area is now less than 4-by-4.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New ruling on a related theme: before, a wall's height was reduced; now, a pillar's area is reduced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any stake driven into a 4-by-4, 10-high pillar in רשות הרבים cancels its 4-by-4 surface.

steps.title: The stake must be three טפחים high
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה limits רב הונא's rule: the stake must be at least 3 טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: This applies only when the stake is three טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה adds a limit to רב הונא's rule. The stake reduces the pillar only if it is at least 3 טפחים tall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something less than 3 טפחים tall is treated as part of the surface under the rule of לבוד. So in his view, a short stake does not count, and the top still counts as a flat 4-by-4 surface.

keyTerms.meaning: Rule that a gap or height under 3 טפחים is treated as joined or flat

phrases.english: And only when it is three handbreadths high.
phrases.notes: Below 3, the rule of לבוד treats the top as level.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: וּבְגָבוֹהַּ שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב הונא's 'stake of any size' to a stake at least 3 טפחים tall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a stake 3 טפחים high reduces the pillar's surface.

steps.title: Even a stake shorter than three reduces it
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא disagree with רב אדא: even a stake under 3 טפחים reduces the pillar.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: Even if the stake is not three טפחים high, it reduces the pillar.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא give the opposite view from רב אדא בר אהבה. In their view, even a short stake cancels the pillar's surface.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps רב הונא's words 'כל שהוא' (any size) exactly as he said them. The reason for their view comes in the next line.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין גָּבוֹהַּ שְׁלֹשָׁה.
phrases.english: Even though it is not three handbreadths high.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב אדא's 3-טפחים limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stake of any height, even under 3 טפחים, reduces the pillar.

steps.title: Why a short stake still counts
steps.stepSummary: The reason for אביי and רבא: once the stake is there, the pillar top cannot really be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because one cannot use it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why אביי and רבא hold their view, and answers right away: with a bump on top, the pillar is no longer usable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 4-by-4 surface counts only because people can put things on it, and that needs a level surface. Even a small bump ruins that. So for אביי and רבא, the question is whether the surface can really be used, not whether it counts as flat under לבוד.

phrases.notes: A surface with a bump is not usable for placing things.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא: לָא מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind אביי and רבא's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does a stake under 3 טפחים reduce the pillar?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the surface can no longer be used.

steps.title: Even a three-טפחים stake does not reduce it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי: even a 3-טפחים stake does not cancel the surface, because you can hang things on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even a stake three טפחים high does not reduce it. What is the reason? It is possible to hang something on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third view. Even a tall stake does not take away the pillar's status, because the stake itself can still be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי uses the same test as אביי and רבא, which is whether the pillar is still usable, but he reaches the opposite result. You can no longer rest things on top, but you can hang things on the stake. So the pillar is still useful and stays a רשות היחיד.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on a stake in a pillar. רב אדא says only a stake of 3 טפחים reduces it, because anything shorter counts as flat under לבוד. אביי and רבא say even a short stake reduces it, because the top cannot be used. רב אשי says even a 3-טפחים stake does not reduce it, because you can hang things on it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a domain's status depends on whether the space can really be used. The views differ only on what counts as 'usable'.

phrases.english: Even if it is three handbreadths high,
phrases.notes: It still does not reduce the pillar.

phrases.english: It is possible to hang something on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁגָּבוֹהַּ שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same 'is it usable?' test as step 9 but reaches the opposite result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a 3-טפחים stake does not cancel the pillar's status, since things can be hung on it.

steps.title: What if the whole pillar top is filled with stakes?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי: according to you, what if the stakes fill the entire top of the pillar?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רבא, said to רב אשי: if he filled it completely with stakes, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A student pushes רב אשי's view to an extreme case. If one stake does not ruin the pillar top, what about stakes covering the whole surface?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said a stake does not cancel the surface because you can still hang things on it, and the rest of the surface can still be used. When stakes cover the entire top, there seems to be no flat space left at all. So the question is whether רב אשי's reasoning still works.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law? (a question asking for a ruling)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
If he filled it entirely with stakes,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִלְּאוֹ כּוּלּוֹ בִּיתֵדוֹת מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב אשי's ruling from Step 10 on an extreme case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a pillar completely covered with stakes still count as a usable surface, according to רב אשי?

steps.title: רב אשי points to רבי יוחנן's rule about a pit and its rim
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers by quoting רבי יוחנן: a pit and its rim combine to reach the ten-טפחים measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did you not hear what רבי יוחנן said? A pit and its rim combine to make up ten.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins his answer by bringing a known ruling about a בור and its חוליא (the stone rim around a pit). He will use it as a model for the stakes case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says the pit and its rim join together to reach the needed size for a private domain. רב אשי is preparing a comparison. The rim around a pit is hard to use, just like a pillar covered in stakes, yet it still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Have you not heard? (introduces a known source)
Its rim or embankment, the stone ring around the mouth of the pit
Combines, joins together to complete a measure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the answer ends here. Quoting רבי יוחנן is only the setup. The actual comparison to the stakes comes in the next step.
steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of Step 11 by citing a parallel ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer will come from רבי יוחנן's rule that a pit and its rim combine, which shows that a hard-to-use area can still count.

steps.title: Just as a board is laid over the pit, a board can be laid over the stakes
steps.stepSummary: The rim of a pit is hard to use, yet it counts because one can lay something across it. The same is true of a pillar covered with stakes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why should the rim count? He cannot use it! Rather, what must you say? That he places an object over it and uses it. Here too, he places an object over the stakes and uses it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his proof. He asks how the pit's rim can count when it cannot be used, answers that one can lay a board across it, and applies the same idea to the stakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'why should it count, he cannot use it?' is rhetorical. It shows that רבי יוחנן must already accept the idea of laying an object across. Once that idea is accepted, a pillar full of stakes is no different. A board can be placed on top of the stakes, so the pillar keeps its status as a usable surface.

keyTerms.meaning: But why? (a challenge to the logic)
Rather, what must you say? (forces the only possible explanation)
Here too (applies the same logic to our case)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, stakes never cancel a pillar's surface, even when they cover all of it. You can always lay something across them and use the top.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a principle: a surface counts as usable if it can easily be made usable by laying an object over it, even if it cannot be used directly as it is.

phrases.english: That he places an object and uses it.
he places an object over the stakes and uses it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי, הָא לָא מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison begun in Step 12 and applies it to the stakes case.
steps.raayaObject: That a pillar fully covered with stakes still counts as a usable surface.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a pit and its rim combine, which only works because one can lay an object across the opening.

steps.title: A ten-handbreadth wall needs a fourteen-handbreadth ladder
steps.stepSummary: Quoting שמואל, רב יהודה rules that a ladder must be fourteen טפחים long to work as a passage over a wall ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a wall ten handbreadths high needs a ladder fourteen handbreadths long to permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to walls between courtyards and asks what kind of ladder turns such a wall into a usable passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wall ten טפחים high normally separates two areas. A ladder leaned against it can make it count as a way across. The ladder has to lean at an angle, not stand straight up, so שמואל requires it to be fourteen טפחים long so that it still reaches the top.

keyTerms.meaning: To permit it, so the wall can be crossed and used
A handbreadth, a unit of measurement

steps.confusionAlert: The ladder is longer than the wall because it leans at an angle. A slanted ladder needs extra length to reach the same height.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
requires a ladder fourteen handbreadths long

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל כּוֹתֶל עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the stakes discussion ends, returns to the theme of steps 1-5: how a ladder lets a person cross a wall between courtyards and so lowers its effective height.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ladder leaned against a ten-טפחים wall must be fourteen טפחים long to count as a passage.

steps.title: רב יוסף: thirteen handbreadths and a bit is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says a ladder of thirteen טפחים and a little more is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: even thirteen handbreadths and a bit is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a smaller measurement than שמואל for how long the ladder must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף holds that the ladder does not have to reach all the way to the top of the wall. Coming within one טפח of the top is close enough. That is why he needs less length than שמואל does.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on the ladder for a ten-טפחים wall. שמואל requires fourteen טפחים. רב יוסף allows thirteen and a bit, because coming close to the top is enough.

phrases.english: Even thirteen and a bit is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר וּמַשֶּׁהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with שמואל's measurement from Step 14 and allows a shorter ladder.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ladder of thirteen טפחים and a bit is enough for a ten-טפחים wall.

steps.title: אביי: eleven טפחים and a bit is enough
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that a ladder of only eleven טפחים and a bit is enough to serve as a passage over a ten-טפחים wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even a ladder of eleven טפחים and a little more is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a third, lower opinion on the minimum ladder length. He goes below both שמואל's 14 and רב יוסף's 13 and a bit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even placed at an angle, an eleven-and-a-bit ladder reaches more than seven טפחים up the wall. That leaves a gap of less than three טפחים to the top, and by the rule of לבוד a gap under three טפחים is treated as closed. So the ladder effectively reaches the top.

keyTerms.meaning: The rule that a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as closed or joined

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the ladder physically reaches the top of the wall. It only needs to come within three טפחים of the top, and לבוד fills in the rest.

phrases.notes: Eleven טפחים and a bit, so the top of the ladder comes within three טפחים of the top of the wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a more lenient minimum length than רב יוסף's 13 and a bit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ladder of eleven טפחים and a bit is a valid passage over a ten-טפחים wall.

steps.title: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: seven טפחים and a bit is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rules that even a ladder of seven טפחים and a bit is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, the son of רב יהושע, said: Even a ladder of seven טפחים and a little more is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth opinion goes lower still, to just over seven טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works only if the ladder stands straight up against the wall instead of leaning at an angle. Standing upright, it reaches above seven טפחים, which is within three טפחים of the top, so לבוד completes the height. The new idea here is that even an upright ladder counts as a passage.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opinion depends on an upright ladder counting as a usable passage. The next steps, the tradition of רב and the explanation of שמואל, show why that is valid.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:

phrases.notes: The ladder stands upright, and לבוד covers the remaining gap of less than three טפחים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes even lower than אביי by allowing the ladder to stand upright.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An upright ladder of seven טפחים and a bit, using לבוד, is a valid passage.

steps.title: רב's tradition: an upright ladder reduces the wall's height
steps.stepSummary: רב reports a tradition that an upright ladder reduces the wall's height, but admits he does not know the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: An upright ladder reduces the height of the wall. I received this as a tradition, but I do not know the reason for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב brings a received tradition that supports the idea of an upright ladder. He openly says he does not know the reason, which sets up שמואל's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An upright ladder is hard to climb, so you might think it does not create a real passage. רב's tradition says it still counts and lowers the effective height of the wall. The missing reason is the gap that שמואל will fill.

keyTerms.meaning: Reduces (the effective height of the wall)
Here: a tradition received from one's teachers

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word גמרא does not mean the Talmud. It means 'I received this as a tradition.'

phrases.notes: It reduces the effective height of the wall, because it creates a passage.

phrases.english: It is a tradition, and I do not know what the reason is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: סוּלָּם זָקוּף — מְמַעֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a tradition matching the idea behind רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע that an upright ladder works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An upright ladder reduces a wall's height. This is a tradition whose reason רב does not know.

steps.title: שמואל explains: like one platform on top of another
steps.stepSummary: שמואל expresses surprise that רב does not know the reason, then explains it by comparing the case to a platform stacked on a platform.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Does אבא (רב) really not know the reason for this? It is just like a platform on top of another platform.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל supplies the reason that רב said he did not know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two stacked platforms are awkward to climb, yet they count as a passage because you can get up them with effort. An upright ladder is the same: it is hard to climb, but possible. So it is a real passage that lowers the wall's height.

keyTerms.meaning: Abba, the personal name of רב
It is just like (introduces a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: A passage does not need to be comfortable to count. If it can be climbed, even with difficulty, as with stacked platforms or an upright ladder, it reduces the wall's height. That is how a ladder as short as 7 טפחים and a bit, standing upright, can work.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדַע אַבָּא טַעְמָא דְּהָא מִלְּתָא?!
phrases.english: And does Abba not know the reason for this matter?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical expression of surprise. אבא is רב's name.

phrases.aramaic: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַאִיצְטְבָא עַל גַּבֵּי אִיצְטְבָא.
phrases.english: It is just like a platform on top of a platform.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא יָדַע אַבָּא טַעְמָא דְּהָא מִלְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the implied question in רב's statement ('I do not know the reason').
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason why an upright ladder reduces the wall's height (implied by רב).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is like a platform on top of a platform. It is climbable with difficulty, which is enough to make it a passage.

steps.title: Babylonian palm trunks do not need to be fixed in place
steps.stepSummary: רבה in the name of רבי חייא rules that palm trunks in בבל count as fixed in place without being attached, because their heaviness holds them down.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רבי חייא: Palm trunks in בבל do not need to be fixed in place. Why? Their heaviness fixes them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling. Palm trunks leaned against the wall in בבל still reduce its height even if no one attached them to the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an object used to reduce a wall's height must be firmly set in place. These trunks are so heavy that no one moves them easily, so their weight alone counts as fixing them.

keyTerms.meaning: Palm trees, here meaning cut palm trunks
Fixing an object permanently in place
Their heaviness fixes them in place

phrases.english: Rabba said that Rabbi Chiyya said:
do not need to be fixed in place.
phrases.notes: They reduce the wall's height as they are.
They are too heavy to be moved casually.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from ladder heights to whether heavy objects need to be fixed in place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Babylonian palm trunks count as fixed because of their weight and need no attachment.

steps.title: Babylonian ladders do not need to be fixed in place
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף in the name of רבי אושעיא gives a parallel ruling: ladders in בבל also count as fixed because of their heaviness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said in the name of רבי אושעיא: Ladders in בבל do not need to be fixed in place. Why? Their heaviness fixes them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second tradition with the same wording, but it is about ladders instead of palm trunks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Babylonian ladders were large and heavy, so this tradition treats them like the palm trunks. The new point is that even an object made to be carried around can count as fixed if it is heavy enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Babylonia, where these heavy objects were common

steps.confusionAlert: Read the two traditions side by side. The wording is almost identical, and the only change is דקלים (palm trunks) versus סולמות (ladders). The next step depends on that difference.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said that Rabbi Oshaya said:
do not need to be fixed in place.

phrases.notes: Babylonian ladders were big and heavy.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel tradition that applies the same reasoning to ladders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Babylonian ladders count as fixed because of their weight and need no attachment.

steps.title: How far each of the two traditions reaches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ladder tradition would include palm trunks all the more. The palm-trunk tradition, however, does not include ladders.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said ladders need no fixing would certainly say the same about palm trunks. But the one who said palm trunks need no fixing meant only palm trunks, not ladders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two traditions and shows exactly where they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Palm trunks are heavy and also placed there to stay, so if heavy ladders count as fixed, trunks surely do (כל שכן). Ladders, even heavy ones, are made to be moved from place to place. So the palm-trunk opinion does not extend to them. The disagreement is only about ladders.
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions agree that Babylonian palm trunks need no fixing. They disagree only about heavy Babylonian ladders.

phrases.english: The one who said ladders do not need fixing,
all the more so palm trunks.
phrases.notes: Trunks are heavy and are also meant to stay in place.

phrases.english: But the one who said palm trunks,

phrases.notes: A ladder is made to be moved around.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר סוּלָּמוֹת כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּקָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the relationship between the two traditions in steps 20 and 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ladder opinion includes palm trunks. The palm-trunk opinion excludes ladders.

steps.title: Two narrow ladders with straw rungs between them
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks רבה about a narrow ladder on each side with weak straw rungs in the middle. Do they combine into one wide ladder?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף asked רבה: If there is a ladder on one side, a ladder on the other side, and straw in the middle, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks רבה a real question (בעיא) about a new case. The question is only set up here, and the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ladder must be four טפחים wide to reduce the wall's height. Each ladder here is less than two טפחים wide. The straw rungs between them cannot hold a person. The question is whether the two ladders still join into one valid four-טפחים ladder.

keyTerms.meaning: Straw, here meaning rungs woven of straw

phrases.english: A ladder on this side and a ladder on that side,
phrases.notes: Each is less than two טפחים wide.

phrases.english: and straw rungs in the middle,
phrases.notes: The straw cannot hold a person's weight.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף מֵרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the required width of a ladder.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether two narrow ladders, joined by straw rungs too weak to stand on, combine into one valid four-טפחים-wide ladder.

steps.title: Straw in the middle does not count because the foot cannot climb on it
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that two narrow ladders with straw rungs between them do not combine, because the foot cannot climb on the straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: The sole of the foot cannot climb on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers רב יוסף's question from the last step. He says no: the ladders do not combine, because a person cannot actually step on the straw in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person usually puts his foot in the middle of a ladder. Here the middle is weak straw, so the ladder may look four טפחים wide but cannot really be used that way. A ladder that cannot really be climbed does not lower the height of the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (introduces the answer)
Does not climb / cannot go up

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ladder fails because it is too narrow on paper. Together it measures four טפחים. It fails only because the part a person really steps on, the middle, is unusable.

phrases.english: The sole of the foot does not climb upon them.
phrases.notes: The foot normally steps in the middle, and the middle here is straw.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין כַּף הָרֶגֶל עוֹלָה בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question asked in step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They do not combine, because the foot cannot climb on the straw in the middle.

steps.title: What if the straw is on the sides and the ladder is in the middle?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף flips the case: straw rungs on each side and a narrow real ladder in the middle. Do they combine?
steps.simpleTranslation: Straw on this side and straw on that side, and a ladder in the middle: what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks a follow-up question that reverses the previous case. Now the strong ladder is in the middle and the weak straw is on the outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real ladder in the middle is narrower than four טפחים. With the straw on both sides added, the total width reaches four טפחים. The question is whether the straw sides can join the middle ladder to make one wide ladder.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (what is the law?)

phrases.english: Straw on this side and straw on that side,
and a ladder in the middle: what is the law?
phrases.notes: The middle ladder alone is less than four טפחים wide.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשִּׁין מִכָּאן וְקַשִּׁין מִכָּאן וְסוּלָּם בָּאֶמְצַע, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the setup of step 23, after רבה's answer in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether straw rungs on the sides join a narrow middle ladder to make a four-טפחים ladder.

steps.title: Ladder in the middle counts because the foot can climb on it
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that this case does count. The foot can climb on the real ladder in the middle, so it combines and lowers the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: Here the sole of the foot does climb on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers yes. Since the strong part is in the middle, where people step, the whole thing counts as one wide ladder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same test decides both cases: can the foot really climb where it normally steps? In the middle, yes, so the ladder looks and works like a four-טפחים ladder. Therefore it lowers the height of the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, indeed (in this case it does)

steps.whatToRemember: One test decides both ladder cases: can the foot climb in the middle? Straw in the middle means no combining. A real ladder in the middle with straw on the sides means the parts combine and lower the wall.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the הלכה follows practical, real use of the ladder, not just how wide it measures.

phrases.english: Here the sole of the foot does climb upon them.
phrases.notes: The real ladder is in the middle, where the foot normally steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲרֵי כַּף הָרֶגֶל עוֹלָה בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 using the same foot-test as step 24, but reaches the opposite result.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They combine, because the foot can climb on the ladder in the middle. So it lowers the height of the wall.
